title: Choose the visual world
question: One screen, one world. The roll assigned Segment Survey; two challengers held their ground and four were declined after weighing. Which world should lanlord be built in?

options.label: Segment Survey
options.lineage: network cartography — plotted segment maps and patch-diagram plates
options.thesis: The segment is drawn as a surveyed line: arrivals above it, departures below, the device register beneath.
options.viewport: A 24-hour change rail across the top of a dense register; presence is a solid mark, absence a hollow one.
options.risk: Cartography drifts into a graph for its own sake; the rail must answer what changed before it decorates.

raised.raise: Visible modular grid: the rail's ticks and the register's columns sit on a drawn armature, not invisible hairlines.
Density as the aesthetic: tighter row rhythm, hairline data graphics, tabular figures throughout.
Empty and degraded states get designed, plain-language copy instead of a hidden paragraph.
State is coded before it is named: a compact legend strip decodes present, departed and new.
Recency carries weight: fresh rows hold heavier ink, stale rows recede without disappearing.
Live and gone are split by one structural rule, so absence has a place on the page, not only a filter.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Every state change is a flap: the board reads as a live arrivals and departures list.
options.viewport: A dark board under a live clock, status cells flipping between present and departed.
options.risk: Its change metaphor is familiar in monitoring UIs, and the flap grammar reads as novelty if it does not carry real state.

options.label: Grid Register
options.thesis: A register built on a visible construction grid, with counts as monumental figures.
options.viewport: Four monumental figures over a register whose columns sit on drawn grid lines, one blue accent.
options.risk: High craft, low identification: the discipline lands, the reference does not.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — the drawn grid gives the register a real armature — but loses on audience identification.
options.kept: Blue accent plane and visible construction grid, adopted as the rail's armature.

options.label: Data Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white, a hairline bar field standing where the change history goes.
options.viewport: A barcode field over a monospace register, the newest arrival inverted to white-on-black.
options.risk: Monochrome density can make the register decorative rather than readable.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on density and tabular figures, but loses on clarity: the bar field competes with the register.
options.kept: Monochrome data density and hairline graphics, adopted into row rhythm.

options.label: Warm Cards
options.thesis: Soft cards on a warm ground, with plain language and one action color.
options.viewport: A single scrolling column of device cards with a bottom bar.
options.risk: Reads as a consumer app, not an operator's register.
options.case: Declined: the operator does not identify with consumer-app softness, and history has no home in a card feed.
options.kept: Plain-language state copy, adopted for empty and degraded states.

options.label: Coded Sleeve
options.thesis: Names replaced by a coded strip of hue blocks that decodes on inspection.
options.viewport: A black field with a stacked white pulse and a small fac number.
options.risk: Coding state instead of labeling it costs clarity on a working screen.
options.case: Declined: clarity fails — an inventory cannot make the visitor decode every row.
options.kept: Coded state strip, adopted as a compact legend that decodes once, not per row.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Devices plotted as magnitude-ranked marks on a coordinate field.
options.viewport: A navy plate with dot-scaled devices and an index of named objects.
options.risk: A coordinate sky has no honest mapping onto a /24 segment.
options.case: Declined: the spatial metaphor is false here, so the mechanism cannot be trusted.
options.kept: Magnitude mapping, adopted as ink weight by recency.

options.label: J-Card
options.thesis: Two hard halves, side A and side B, ruled in ballpoint with running times.
options.viewport: A folded card listing tracks with times right-aligned to the margin.
options.risk: Handwriting is a costume on a read-only tool.
options.case: Declined: identification holds, but the lettering is costume and the two halves are the only real mechanism.
options.kept: The hard two-way split, adopted as the structural rule between live and gone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean monitoring dashboard: summary cards, a filterable table, green and red presence dots.
canonCard.viewport: Four status cards over a sortable table with a search field.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other LAN dashboard; says nothing about history.
